Subject: Packaging questions and upgrade flexibility for pilot

Hi Sergio / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look promising. We're mapping out how Redwood would fit into Needle Health's inference footprint and have a couple of questions about packaging and upgrade/downgrade rules before we take this to Procurement. High level:

- We'll likely start with a 3-month pilot (hosted API + small dedicated pool) and then either scale into Dedicated or keep hosted if economics work.
- Need clarity on how seat/throughput bundles convert when we upgrade mid-contract (e.g., pilot -> reserved Dedicated capacity). Do we credit unused hosted usage or prorate?
- How do feature bundles (streaming, function-calls, higher retention for cache) map into tiers — can they be toggled without re-contracting?

Procurement also asked for a rough pricing grid for 1k / 10k / 100k monthly token volumes so they can model cost. Can you share an example pricing table plus any standard discount bands for pilots that convert?

We have a procurement timeline that looks like: pilot sign SOW by 7/30, procurement review 8/5, signed by 8/15. If we can get a proposed MAP and the grid this week it would help.

Thanks,
Maya Gupta
Director of ML Platforms
Needle Health

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Follow-ups inline and a proposed next step below.

On credits/proration: short answer — we provide a conversion credit for hosted usage when a customer moves that consumption into a Dedicated reserved contract, calculated on actual billed tokens over the pilot period and applied to the first billing cycle of the Dedicated commitment. Typical mechanics: we compute the billed hosted spend during the pilot, apply a conversion factor (usually 70–90% depending on discount band) as a one-time credit. We can show sample math in the pricing grid.

On toggling features: feature flags like streaming and function-call support are enabled at the API layer and do not require re-contracting. Add-ons that change billing (e.g., higher cache retention, longer KV TTLs that increase memory footprint) are considered billable add-ons and are priced on a per-capacity basis; toggling them during a billing period will be handled with pro-rated charges and visible in the Console.

Upgrade workflow (pilot -> Dedicated):
- Pilot SOW (hosted + pilot Dedicated slice if requested)
- MAP due within 48 hours of proposal (we'll attach a filled template)
- Conversion review: we reconcile billed hosted usage, calculate credit, and issue invoice offset on month 1 of Dedicated term
- If customer upgrades mid-billing cycle, we'll pro-rate capacity and apply the conversion credit at next invoice run

I've attached our packaging overview and a starter MAP. Ben, can you drop a sample pricing grid with discount bands (pilot convert %, 3/6/12-month commit tiers) and guidance on one-off concession levers (intro discount, onboarding credit)? Lauren, looping you for approval on the pilot concession ranges (we typically keep entrance discounts in the 10–20% window for pilot-to-Dedicated conversions).

Next step: propose a 45 min packaging workshop this Thursday 7/21 at 10am PT to walk Needle's procurement/infra through options and show the MAP flow. If that works we'll send a calendar invite + short pre-read.

Thanks,
— Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Sergio — quick pricing note to bring to the workshop.

Attached: pricing-grid-qty-breaks.xlsx (pricing bands + illustrative math)

Key points to surface to Needle Health:
- Pilot credits: offer a 15% conversion uplift for pilots that sign a 12-month Dedicated commit within 60 days of pilot end. This means we credit 85% of pilot hosted spend toward the first month of Dedicated.
- Short-term pilots (<=3 months) get a standard onboarding credit of $10k to help with migration and eval tooling; can be structured as a rebate on first invoice.
- Volume breaks: 0-10k tokens, 10k-100k, 100k-1M. Provide per-token unit prices in the sheet.
- One-off concessions: we can grant a one-time migration discount equal to 5% of first-quarter billing for strategic accounts; requires sales manager sign-off.

Also recommend calling out rollback criteria in the SOW: if Needle downgrades within the first 90 days of Dedicated term, we apply a shortfall recovery which is the difference between committed spend and actual usage, pro-rated to remaining term — but we include a one-time forgiveness buffer equal to one month of committed spend for enterprise goodwill.

I'll be on the workshop to walk the math. Sergio — want me to prepare two slide rows: (A) conservative convert case, (B) aggressive convert case (with expanded credits)?

Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
